body: For auto OEMs and suppliers, company-reported monthly 'sales' are factory despatches to dealers (wholesale). Vahan registrations, aggregated by FADA, are retail to end customers. When wholesale runs ahead of retail for several months, dealer inventory builds up. Dealer inventory days are quoted in FADA's monthly releases. That has historically come before production cuts and discounting, which hit margins and the suppliers' order flow. Retail running ahead of wholesale points to inventory depletion and restocking upside. Method: track a 3-month rolling sum of each OEM's Vahan registrations against its reported despatches, and alert when the gap passes 10–15% or when FADA's inventory days exceed roughly 45–50 for PVs. Small-cap ancillaries get their volume signal from their top OEM customers' retail data before their own results appear. The threshold is a working heuristic, not back-tested here.
title: Retail (Vahan/FADA) vs wholesale (SIAM/company despatch) gap as an early warning
